summary: Final report MV-2018-052 for Avernelwick Pharma: Microsomal CLint, fu,p by equilibrium dialysis on 40 compounds (Aminopyrimidine regioisomer). Study summary table on page 1; full compound tables, methods, controls and deviations follow.

title_block.title: AP02 clearance and free-fraction assessment, recovery-controlled dialysis
title_block.subtitle: Final Report
lines: Study lead: Dr M. Larkin, DMPK Study Director

blocks.p: 40 compounds from the Avernelwick aminopyrimidine regioisomer series 02 were tested for Avernelwick Pharma in the Microsomal CLint, fu,p by equilibrium dialysis. Testing started on March 12, 2018 and results were reported on April 16, 2018. All accepted runs met matrix acceptance criteria.
To rank the test article set for Microsomal CLint, fu,p by equilibrium dialysis liability so that Avernelwick Pharma could choose analogues for progression.

40 compounds were received as 10 mM DMSO solutions in one accession lot on March 12, 2018 and logged against M18/BIO/01223. Identity and concentration were taken as supplied by the client. Stocks were stored at -20 °C and thawed once for testing.

Test articles (1 µM) were incubated with pooled human and rat liver microsomes (0.5 mg/mL protein) at 37 °C with NADPH (1 mM); a no-NADPH control at 45 minutes checks for non-metabolic loss. Samples at 0, 5, 15, 30 and 45 minutes are quenched in acetonitrile with internal standard and analyzed by LC-MS/MS. CLint is calculated from the first-order depletion slope. When depletion over 45 minutes is below the quantifiable limit, CLint is reported as an upper bound (<3 µL/min/mg) and half-life as a lower bound (>60 min).
Matrix acceptance: verapamil (high clearance) and diltiazem (moderate clearance) within 0.5-2 times their historical CLint in each run; no-NADPH loss below 15%.

Binding to human plasma was measured by rapid equilibrium dialysis (5 µM test article, 4 h at 37 °C, PBS pH 7.4). Plasma and buffer compartments are matrix-matched before LC-MS/MS. Results are reported as percent bound and percent unbound with mass-balance recovery; recoveries below 70% are footnoted.
Warfarin is included as the binding control in every plate (acceptance: 97-99.5% bound).

table.caption: Table 2 Microsomal intrinsic clearance and half-life

blocks.p: No deviations from the study plan.

Microsomal clearance varied across the set and between species. Plasma binding should be considered with clearance when ranking exposure potential. Values are in vitro and do not by themselves predict clinical risk; free exposure estimates are needed for that assessment.
Recommended next steps: take the lower-clearance analogues into hepatocyte or in vivo follow-up.
Raw data, assay worksheets and instrument files are retained for 5 years under M18/BIO/01223.
